title: The Compute Lease
primary_metric: total infrastructure cost per GPU-hour delivered to paying customers over the 24-month evaluation window, summed as a series under each growth-rate scenario

options.A: The Long Lock — sign a fixed-rate, multi-year GPU cluster lease
options.B: The Open Tap — buy on-demand GPU capacity that scales with actual customer growth

_ext: keys below are pipeline extensions, additive to SPEC §4
protagonist: Sofia Reyes, Infrastructure Capacity Planner, Kestrel Compute

deliverables.text: A monthly GPU-hour demand sequence: recursive rule and closed form, months 1-24, low/mid/high growth scenarios.
Two 24-month total-cost series (Long Lock, Open Tap), written as explicit sums, term by term.
Convergence/divergence classification of the Open Tap's monthly-cost series extended past 24 months, with the common ratio identified.
Total cost per GPU-hour delivered, both options, all three growth scenarios (six results in one table).
The crossover growth rate at which both series' 24-month totals produce the same cost per GPU-hour delivered.
A recommendation to the board, defended with D4 and D5, including what would have to be true for the recommendation to be wrong.

appendices.title: Kestrel's Board Directive and Decision Constraints
The Long Lock — 3-Year Fixed-Rate GPU Cluster Lease
The Open Tap — On-Demand GPU Capacity

balance.argument_a: The Long Lock's fixed per-GPU-hour rate is lower than any on-demand rate Kestrel could get, and that gap compounds favorably the more GPU-hours actually get used over 24 months — if Kestrel's growth lands near the mid or high end of Appendix D's range, the fixed cost gets spread over enough usage that its cost-per-GPU-hour-delivered undercuts the Open Tap even though the Open Tap's own rate never changes.
balance.argument_b: The Open Tap's total cost is a series that tracks real usage exactly — it never pays for GPU-hours nobody rents. If Kestrel's growth lands near the low end of Appendix D's range (or undershoots it), the Long Lock keeps billing its full fixed series regardless, including the months of committed contract that run past the 24-month evaluation window, while the Open Tap's series stays proportional to whatever demand actually showed up.
balance.margin_basis: Once Appendices B, C, and D are sourced: sum each option's 24-month cost series (D2), divide by total GPU-hours delivered over the same window, for each of the low/mid/high growth scenarios (D4). The margin is the percent difference between the two options' cost-per-GPU-hour-delivered at the scenario closest to Kestrel's actual expected growth rate, and D5's crossover-rate calculation shows how sensitive that margin is to which end of Appendix D's range Kestrel actually experiences.
